source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Why does seat-minder look up student names and photos from a roster at runtime instead of hard-coding them into the program?

options.text: Hard-coding names and photos would make the app run noticeably slower
options.feedback: Speed is not the reason given. The reasoning is about privacy, and about a habit worth keeping whenever an agent handles personal data.

options.text: Runtime lookups of this kind are required by the Vercel hosting platform
options.feedback: No hosting requirement of this kind is mentioned; the practice is described as a general good habit, not a constraint of the platform.

options.text: It keeps personal data out of the code itself, by design
options.feedback: The program knows only that a roster and a set of images exist somewhere it can read, which is the same privacy-by-design pattern this course's own FERPA-safe roster tooling uses.

options.text: It lets the app work for a student not yet added to the roster
options.feedback: Missing roster entries are not discussed. The stated reason is keeping personal data out of the program rather than covering an edge case.
